profile.headline: IoT & ML Engineer | Turning AIoT Research into Deployable Systems
profile.summary:
Most CS students spend their degree studying systems. I spend mine building them.
As a Research Assistant and Technical Support at Acadia University's AIoT Research Hub, I work on real deployed hardware — not simulations, not toy datasets. Real sensors. Real environments. Real problems.
I designed and built a compost monitoring system from scratch — integrating CO₂, temperature, and humidity sensors to collect live environmental data for research analysis. I'm currently prototyping a LoRaWAN wireless sensor network for greenhouse monitoring, taking it through hardware design, firmware, and testing toward full deployment.
Beyond building, I run lab operations, organize workshops, and mentor students as a Teaching Assistant — because I think understanding something deeply means being able to teach it clearly.
My stack: Python · C++ · LoRaWAN · MQTT · Embedded Systems · IoT Protocols · ML Pipelines
I'm a 3rd-year Computer Science student at Acadia University, actively looking for Summer 2026 internships in IoT Engineering, Software Engineering, or ML Engineering.
If you're building at the edge of AI and physical systems — let's connect.

projects.title: LoRaWAN Wireless Sensor Network for Greenhouse Monitoring
projects.description:
Designing and building a low-power wireless sensor network for real-time greenhouse environmental monitoring using LoRaWAN — a long-range, low-power IoT protocol built for exactly this kind of deployed field application.
Working independently under faculty supervision at the Acadia AIoT Research Hub, I am developing firmware on the STM32WL55JC1 — a microcontroller with an integrated LoRa radio — to acquire environmental readings from a BME280 sensor (temperature, pressure, humidity) and transmit them wirelessly through a SenseCAP M2 LoRaWAN gateway to a cloud platform for storage and analysis.
This project covers the full embedded IoT stack: sensor integration, low-level firmware development, wireless protocol configuration, and gateway-to-cloud pipeline setup — all on production-grade hardware targeting real greenhouse deployment.
Key contributions:
→ Selected and integrated BME280 sensor for multi-parameter environmental sensing (temperature, humidity, pressure)
→ Writing low-level firmware in C/C++ for the STM32WL55JC1, a dual-core MCU with integrated sub-GHz LoRa radio
→ Configuring LoRaWAN stack for reliable long-range wireless transmission to SenseCAP M2 gateway
→ Architecting end-to-end data pipeline from sensor node → LoRaWAN gateway → cloud storage
→ Conducting prototype testing in preparation for live greenhouse deployment

projects.title: IoT Compost Monitoring System with ML-Driven Analysis
projects.description:
Built a full end-to-end IoT pipeline that collects real environmental data from compost and feeds it into a machine learning model for prediction and analysis — bridging embedded hardware, wireless data transmission, and applied ML in a single research system.
My role — Hardware & Firmware (ESP32 · C/C++):
Integrated a DS18B20 temperature sensor and SCD40 CO₂/humidity sensor onto an ESP32 microcontroller, writing firmware in C/C++ to continuously capture compost temperature, ambient temperature, CO₂, and humidity readings. Engineered the data pipeline to stream live sensor data to ThingSpeak, a cloud IoT platform, for persistent storage and real-time visualization.
Partner's role — ML & Data Analysis (Claire):
Using the dataset collected by the sensor system, my research partner applied machine learning models to perform environmental predictions and data analysis on compost behaviour over time.
This project represents a complete AIoT workflow — from physical sensor to cloud to intelligent analysis.
Key contributions:
→ Integrated DS18B20 + SCD40 sensors on ESP32 for multi-parameter environmental monitoring
→ Wrote C/C++ firmware for reliable continuous data acquisition and transmission
→ Configured ThingSpeak pipeline for real-time cloud data logging and visualization
→ Co-designed the system architecture that enabled downstream ML analysis

publications.title: Developing a New IoT Network Topology for Effective Greenhouse Monitoring and Control
publications.description: Greenhouses provide a controlled environment that supports optimal plant growth by controlling key environmental conditions. However, traditional greenhouse systems face challenges such as real-time data collection and monitoring of accurate environmental parameters. IoT is becoming a critical tool in addressing these concerns and optimizing environmental monitoring in greenhouses. This paper presents an IoT-based Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) for smart greenhouse monitoring. The system is implemented at the K.C. Irving Environmental Science Centre in Wolfville, NS. It integrates Crossbow Iris Motes with sensors for temperature, humidity, and light to collect and transmit real-time environmental data. The system uses a Raspberry Pi as a processing hub to clean and modify data before it is sent to InfluxDB, which acts as a central server for accessing and storing the data. Grafana is used next for data visualization and analytics. Additionally, we discuss the potential for integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the system. This includes predictive analytics to support decision-making and automation, as well as anomaly detection to ensure smooth system operation. Our system addresses key limitations of existing systems by improving scalability and real-time responsiveness. It also lays the groundwork for future project iterations through the integration of expanded sensor networks and AI. This work contributes to the advancement of smart agriculture by using IoT to enable energy-efficient, data-driven greenhouse management that supports plant growth and health.

publications.title: Comparative Analysis of Scalable IoT Topologies for Optimal and Precise Greenhouse Environment Monitoring
publications.description: Precision agriculture is vital for optimizing parameters for plant growth and health particularly in controlled environments like greenhouses. The Internet of Things (IoT) is a driver of this, and Wireless Sensor Networks provide a structured approach for data acquisition in these environments. While WSNs are widely implemented, there is limited empirical comparison of signal performance metrics across different sensor motes. This study presents a comparative analysis using the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) parameter of two different IoT devices, Iris Mote and Zolertia RE-Mote in a greenhouse environment, specifically at the K.C. Irving Environmental Science Centre Greenhouse at Acadia University. Results indicate that the Zolertia RE-Mote offers superior range, processing power, and energy efficiency, making it better suited for scalable deployments. These findings highlight the importance of environment specific testing for WSN deployment in precision agriculture.
